A companion paper details validation on a calcium-binding protein, yielding crystallographic structures and measurable binding, with in-house synthesis achieving a 71% cost reduction over catalog purchasing, labor and consumables included. Reactant rather than product procurement gives potentially 2.5 times as many accessible compounds and higher interaction productivity for the same budget. Syndirella is most impactful for structure-enabled campaigns with fragment-bound crystal structures, robust HT chemistry, and assays compatible with crude reaction mixtures, and is available at https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella. Syndirella proposes elaborations of fragment-derived scaffolds for high-throughput synthesis using in-catalog reactants for SAR exploration.
full_text_sections.methods: MethodsSyndirella takes as input fragment or fragment-derived scaffold structures and outputs congeneric series with 3D poses and associated synthetic routes suitable for HT synthesis. For each scaffold, synthetic routes are first solved using a retrosynthesis tool or defined manually, and for each required reactant, a superstructure search is performed under constraints that preserve the reaction site. The resulting reactant superstructures are combined to yield a large set of elaborated products, which are then energy-minimized in silico into the experimental protein structure with strong constraints to the experimental fragment pose using Fragmenstein.51 Predicted conformations are subsequently scored and filtered based on geometry checks and modeled binding energy. The pipeline is tunable and expandable to accommodate the specific capabilities and preferences of downstream HT synthesis experiments.Computational workflowSyndirella produces congeneric series of compounds from input scaffolds with fragment origin. These scaffolds can be fragments themselves or derivatives from fragment growing, linking, or most commonly in this work, fragment merges.52 Fragment merged compounds can be proposed algorithmically or manually, although design methods should prioritize the recapitulation of fragment atoms. One algorithmic method that implements fragment merging and is extensively used throughout our pipeline is Fragmenstein.51 Fragmenstein combines atoms from fragments using structural information to create derivatives that are predicted to adopt the same binding pose as the fragments. Additionally, Wills et al. utilized the Fragment Network,53,54 first described by Astex Pharmaceuticals,15 where traversing a graph database of compounds starting from a fragment node leads to derivative compounds that recapitulate fragment–protein interactions. Compounds that are used as input into the complete Syndirella workflow are hereafter referred to as scaffolds, shown in Fig. 1.Fig. 1Workflow of Syndirella starting from a fragment-inspired scaffold, the pipeline defines synthetic routes, identifies superstructures of reactants from chemical catalogs, predicts products via combinatorial synthesis, and performs placement relative to inspiration fragments using Fragmenstein.51 The example shows a two-step synthesis (amidation and Suzuki coupling) where final products (thick representation) are overlaid with original fragments (thin representation), with successful placements indicated by green checkmarks and not successful by red crosses.Pose generation of scaffolds and filteringFirst, poses are generated for input scaffolds to filter out those which do not have an energetically favorable conformation in the binding site. Pose generation is performed using the tool Fragmenstein,51 although any pose generation method could be used, whether restrained to the parent fragment pose or not. Fragmenstein generates an initial pose by calculating the positional overlap between the compound and fragments used for the original merge. The atoms on the compound found in this overlap are restricted to the coordinates from the fragments. This unphysical conformation undergoes energy minimization placed in the apo protein template specified by the user. Energy minimization is controlled by either PyRosetta's scorefunction ref2015 (ref. 55) or RDKit's UFF.56 For the analysis shown here, minimization with RDKit's UFF was performed unless specified otherwise. When using PyRosetta, the sidechains of protein residues with alpha carbons within 8 Å of the centroid of the compound are energy minimized whereas the protein is fixed when performing UFF minimization. A ΔΔG score is calculated by Fragmenstein as a single snapshot difference of the final bound state minus the unbound state (see ref. 51). It should be mentioned that this ΔΔG score should not be interpreted as a robust free binding energy and instead is used only as a filter where if the score is ≥0 the pose is most likely energetically unfavorable and strained.Scaffolds that complete energy minimization within 240 s, have an RMSD of <2 Å to the inspiration fragments, have a ΔΔG score of <0, and pass PoseBuster's intramolecular geometry checks for bond lengths, angles, steric clashes, and aromatic ring planarity are accepted.57Route modeling for HT synthesisFor each scaffold that passes pose generation, Syndirella proposes elaborations by explicit SMIRKS-encoded forward synthesis route modelling with any number of reaction steps.58 First, route selection is specified for the scaffold manually or proposed by a retrosynthesis tool. Here in this analysis using Manifold (https://postera.ai/), although functionality using the open-source tool AiZynthFinder is also provided. When using Manifold, the catalogs specified to query were enamine_bb, mcule, mcule_ultimate, enamine_real, enamine_made, and generic (common molecules that are found in most catalogs).59–61 For a compound to be considered “elaboratable”, there must be a forward synthesis route with all reactions encoded in Syndirella's SMIRKS library. Syndirella includes 109 SMIRKS encoded reactions which have been specifically chosen for HT chemistry. In this work 23 were used (available as RXN_SMIRKS_CONSTANTS.json on Zenodo62) and since this analysis, more have been added with a significant amount from Dobbelaere et al.63 and are found at https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella.Syndirella prioritizes user synthesis preferencesSyndirella's reaction repertoire can be expanded or edited by adding a SMIRKS pattern58 representing the reaction of interest (e.g., sourced from resources such as SMARTS-RX64 or SmartReact65). Additionally, reaction substitutions can be specified to suit user preferences based on better yield history or usually cheaper reactants. For example, replacing Schotten–Baumann reactions with amidations often improves building block availability and reduces cost (Fig. S4). Each alternative reaction generates an additional and separate synthesis route and can be specified in a .json format and example jupyter notebooks to generate these files are provided (see https://github.com/oxpig/syndirella).Superstructure search of reactants to produce elaborated productsTo produce the series, each reactant in the forward synthesis route is elaborated and the full Cartesian product of the reactants is computed in silico. The following steps are taken for each reaction step in the forward synthesis route. First, the original reactants are labeled with the specific reactant number in the SMIRKS of that reaction. Then, each reactant is used as a query in a superstructure search – performed by Manifold in this work, although functionality using the catalog search tool Arthor (https://arthor.docking.org/) is provided. A superstructure of a query compound is a compound that contains the query compound as a maximum common substructure. In this analysis, the catalogs queried were enamine_bb, mcule, mcule_ultimate, enamine_real, enamine_made, and generic (common molecules that are found in most catalogs).59–61Superstructure reactants are filtered by removing duplicates, compounds containing non-abundant isotopes, compounds that don't match the reactant SMIRKS, and if the number of atom difference to the query reactant is <0 or >10 (although these thresholds can be changed to user preferences). If the step is a bimolecular reaction, reactants that contain both reacting groups are excluded to reduce selectivity issues.Product compounds are generated from the full Cartesian product of the smallest 100 reactants for bimolecular reactions or by the smallest 10 K reactants for unimolecular reactions, thereby restricting the total number of products in each step to ≤10 K (although this threshold can be changed to user preferences). For each reactant combination, the product is determined by the original SMIRKS reaction pattern. Products are excluded if they cannot be sanitized by the RDKit.66 If…
full_text_sections.results: ResultsWe tested the ability of Syndirella to propose elaborations around fragments and fragment merged scaffolds for three viral protein targets: CHIKV-Mac, EV-A71-2A, and EV-D68-3C-PROA. First, we assess the chemical and pharmacophore diversity of the elaboration series produced by Syndirella, resulting in binding site interaction exploration where elaborations recapitulate known fragment interactions and introduce novel interactions with functionally relevant residues. We then show how Syndirella can be used to make decisions on improving the experimental platform's repertoire of synthetic capabilities by identifying critical chemistry needed to expand series accessibility and the tunability of synthesis parameters. Through comparison with traditional superstructure search methods, we show how Syndirella accesses distinct regions of chemical space. Additionally we demonstrate that Syndirella enables a reactant-based purchasing strategy resulting in a broader chemical space exploration and higher predicted interaction productivity within typical budget constraints and outside of the catalog. Finally, the practical utility of the platform is validated through application to NCS-1, where over 400 Syndirella elaborations were accessible via reactant procurement compared with only two via direct product procurement. These elaborations were synthesized by HT in-house chemistry, resulting in resolved crystal structures and measurable binding kinetics for real-world SAR analysis.Syndirella produces congeneric series with pharmacophore diversity enabling binding site explorationSyndirella produces diverse congeneric series—sets of compounds that share a common core structure but differ in their substituents—using explicit synthesis routes. Fig. 2 shows a representative result, where a single fragment-inspired scaffold yields a set of elaborations that share one synthesis route and vary in substituents and pharmacophores. For this CHIKV-Mac series, the scaffold is a fragment-merged compound and utilizes a single step Buchwald–Hartwig amination reaction to produce 5085 elaborated products (Fig. 2a). The series is pharmacophorically diverse as seen in Fig. 2b with examples of hydrogen bond acceptors, donors, halogens, and hydrophobic groups introduced at four unique R positions on the scaffold.Fig. 2Syndirella produces a SAR series with pharmacophore diversity enabling binding site exploration. This series was designed for the CHIKV-Mac target. (a) The synthesis route (a single step Buchwald–Hartwig amination route) is shown for the scaffold and the four R positions from which the elaborations (n = 5085) vary on. (b) Heatmap of the pharmacophores introduced at the four R positions shown in (a), grouped into hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA), hydrogen bond donors (HBD), halogens, and hydrophobic groups and concatenated with their distance to the attachment point. The percent value shown is the percent of the pharmacophore-distance feature at each R position over the whole compound set. (c) The experimentally resolved structure of the inspiration fragments and hydrogen bond (H-bond) interactions identified by the protein–ligand interaction profiler83 shown by colored circles and labeled by their Fragalysis ID. Each H-bond interaction is outlined by the pharmacophore color matching the pharmacophore heatmap. (d) The predicted pose of the fragment merged scaffold calculated with Fragmenstein and predicted hydrogen bond interactions. (e) Fragmenstein predicted poses of 100 randomly sampled elaborations with five example elaborations shown in 2D, colored by the maximum common substructure with the scaffold, and predicted H-bond interactions shown.The inspiration fragments resulted in two H-bond interactions experimentally resolved with ARG 144 and CYS 143, while the scaffold was predicted to interact with ARG 144 and TYR 142. Across the five example elaborations shown, additional predicted interactions emerge with MET 9 and VAL 33, demonstrating how the elaboration process can potentially expand the interaction profile beyond the original fragment hits.Syndirella's systematic combinatorial enumeration achieves comparable pharmacophore coverage to early-stage experimental FBDD campaigns. In Fig. 3, the pharmacophore-distance heatmaps for Syndirella versus the COVID Moonshot series from the TRY-UNI-714a760b-6 scaffold show similar exploration patterns.84 The COVID Moonshot compounds represent initial follow-ups synthesized within the first four months since the start of the consortium, making them directly comparable to Syndirella's proposed first-iteration elaborations. While Syndirella's automated enumeration cannot match the full diversity of human and computer-designed compounds, it captures similar pharmacophoric positions prioritized in practice, demonstrating its utility as a tool for SAR exploration.Fig. 3Syndirella's systematic approach is comparable with COVID Moonshot's heterogeneous design strategies in pharmacophore space. (a) Pharmacophore-distance heatmap for Syndirella-generated compounds (n = 8685) from the TRY-UNI-714a760b-6 scaffold, showing concentrated pharmacophore clustering at specific R positions. (b) Pharmacophore-distance heatmap for COVID Moonshot compounds (n = 78) from the 3-amino-pyridine like series made in the first four months since the start of the consortium (2020-03-17 to 2020-06-31). (c) Chemical structure of the TRY-UNI-714a760b-6 scaffold with R position labels (R1–R9). Heatmap intensity represents the percentage of compounds containing each pharmacophore type at each distance position. HBA = hydrogen bond acceptor, HBD = hydrogen bond donor.For all series produced by Syndirella in this study, on average, a series contains over 61 unique R-groups after R-group decomposition (Fig. S2a). To provide another diversity metric of all series, the Tanimoto similarity distributions for CHIKV-Mac, EV-A71-2A, and EV-D68-3C-PROA are shown in Fig. S12–S19. Most demonstrate similar diversity profiles to the exemplar hit TRY-UNI-714a760b-6 (Fig. S11) where either the modes are similar to this series (∼0.2). While there are also less diverse series (mode > 0.4) these series usually have an order of magnitude less compounds than the 2 K present in the TRY-UNI exemplar series.Elaborations are predicted to explore new functionally relevant interactions not measured in the fragment screenSyndirella elaborations are predicted to systematically explore the binding site's interaction landscape beyond what traditional fragment merging approaches can capture, recapitulating interactions with residues in the original crystallographic screen and identifying interactions with functionally relevant residues that were not measured. Seen in Fig. 4 the interaction exploration from the original fragment screen to fragment inspirations used for scaffold design and Syndirella generated elaborations is shown for CHIKV-Mac (Fig. 2). From the crystallographic fragment screen,73 there were 109 fragments resolved interacting with 73 unique residues. The predicted interactions for the sub-selected fragments for scaffold design (inspirations) and the scaffolds themselves is reduced compared to the fragment screen due to the subselection, but the frequency and diversity of predicted interactions increases dramatically with the elaborations, which are predicted to interact with 14 residues not found to interact in the original fragment screen (seen grouped in Fig. 4).Fig. 4Syndirella elaborations explore both interactions resolved in the fragment screen and with new functionally relevant residues. Residue interactions measured from the crystallographic fragment screen (fragments), and predicted interactions for the scaffold inspiration fragments (inspirations), scaffolds, and elaborations are shown. The frequency of interactions of all compounds are shown in the bar chart on top. Residues are grouped by functionally relevant residues,85,86 residues where interactions were…
full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionWe have demonstrated that Syndirella systematically generates pharmacophorically diverse congeneric series that enable comprehensive SAR exploration from crystallographic fragment screens. Through analysis of multiple targets (CHIKV-Mac, EV-A71-2A, EV-D68-3C-PROA) and experimental validation with NCS-1,50 our method produces series that are predicted to sample new binding site interactions relative to inspiration fragments. As exemplified with CHIKV-Mac, elaborations resulted in a predicted interaction with the functionally important residue GLY 32, not measured in the fragment screen (Fig. 4). While providing less pharmacophore coverage than real-world heterogeneous approaches like in the COVID Moonshot (Fig. 3), this systematic enumeration offers a tractable method for SAR studies supported by HT chemistry.The NCS-1 experimental case study (detailed in Muñoz-Reyes et al.50) and the more detailed SAR analysis shown here, demonstrated how Syndirella was used for preliminary SAR elucidation. For one scaffold, both favorable pharmacophores (hydrogen bond acceptors/donors at R3 and R4) and unfavorable modifications (hydrophobic groups at R1 preventing crystallization) were identified. This experimental validation shows how Syndirella is used to help understand SAR early in the drug design process, such as identifying activity cliffs and position-specific functional group effects.95,96However, the brute-force combinatorial approach of reactants has inherent limitations that we address through conservative risk management strategies. The static 10 K elaboration threshold used in this work creates tradeoffs where scaffolds accommodate either few R-positions (<4) with many unique groups (>100) or vice versa (Fig. S10). To manage synthetic and design risk—which we define as positively correlating with atoms added relative to scaffolds, encompassing uncertainty about whether elaborations will be successfully synthesized, adopt inspiration fragment conformations, or exhibit measurable biological effects51,97—we prioritize compounds with fewer novel atoms. Since scaffolds already differ from constituent fragments through merging, this conservative threshold maintains lower risk while necessarily excluding larger functional groups. Future iterations could implement position-specific elaboration or variable thresholds.A key strength of Syndirella lies in leveraging established medicinal chemistry reactions while providing unprecedented user flexibility for HT workflows. Analysis reveals 74% of successful routes incorporate at least one of the top five medicinal chemistry reactions identified by Brown and Boström:87 amide formation, Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, SNAr, Boc protection/deprotection, and electrophile–amine reactions. While Syndirella uses SMIRKS to represent reactions, these patterns only capture connectivity and cannot encapsulate the complexities of real-world synthesis such as solubility, by-product formation, chemoselectivity, and regioselectivity. This is a limitation of template-based transformations generally,98 and predicting these outcomes in silico remains an open and active area.99Syndirella nonetheless offers flexibility absent from existing enumeration tools,40,41,100 allowing users to encode specific chemistry workflows, modify retrosynthetic routes, and select cost-effective reactants. A natural extension of this flexibility is to inform it with experimental synthesis outcomes. These outcomes could be analyzed to identify reactant features associated with synthetic success or failure. Such features could be encoded as route or reactant filters within Syndirella's existing preference framework, allowing the synthetic experience captured in one campaign to constrain and prioritize the routes proposed for the next. Curated SMARTS libraries such as SMARTS-RX64 already support this, flagging building blocks that match more than one reactive pattern, such as an amine intended for amide coupling that also carries a second amine or a carboxylic acid, and so risk poor regioselectivity or side products.When compared to catalog-based approaches under similar constraints, Syndirella demonstrates superior breadth-to-depth ratio of scaffold congeneric series (Fig. S5). Despite generating fewer total elaborations due to the 10 K limit in this work, Syndirella produces 26.5% more products per scaffold than Arthor and 47.9% more than Manifold under similar restrictions (Table S1). This superior depth-to-breadth ratio (Fig. S5) proves crucial for early development, where comprehensive scaffold sampling prevents premature limitation to low-performing series.The practical advantages of reactant-based synthesis are not limited to cost. With a 230% increase in accessible compounds through reactant purchasing versus direct procurement (Table 2), Syndirella enables access to chemical space around scaffolds that is absent from commercial catalogs, consistent with the observations of Luttens et al.16 At a 10 K EUR budget and including the realistic constraints of in-house synthesis cost and synthesis failure, this strategy provides access to 356 compounds compared to 144 through direct purchase (Fig. S8), and these estimates are in line with NCS-1 costs of 42.10 EUR per compound for synthesis versus 147.93 EUR per compound from MCule. Reactant-based purchasing also lessens a campaign's dependency on supplier capacity for synthesis as only building-block availability is required. Changes in a supplier's capacity, pricing, or lead times can therefore be accommodated by sourcing reactants from a different supplier. Synthesis performed in-house additionally accumulates expertise within the group, which outsourcing does not, so subsequent campaigns benefit from chemistry the group has already run.This approach carries upfront equipment costs that the per-compound figures above do not capture. The synthesis costs presented come from technician, reagent, and consumables costs (Table S4) and do not include the costs of establishing robotic synthesis capabilities, estimated to total 36 600.00 EUR, see Table S3. The largest costs are the liquid-handling robot (here from Opentrons https://opentrons.com/) and the reactor labware for temperature control, contributing 33% and 53% respectively to the total equipment cost. For a laboratory already undertaking synthesis, these are the main additional equipment investments.Because the upfront equipment cost is amortized across projects, its per-compound contribution falls as more compounds are synthesized. For the overlapping set of 708 products available both by direct purchase and by synthesis from reactants under 100 EUR (Table S2), the reactant route costs 48.12 EUR per compound (reactant price plus 6.11 EUR synthesis cost) versus 88.11 EUR per compound to purchase directly, a saving of approximately 40 EUR per compound. At this estimated saving, the upfront equipment cost of 36 600.00 EUR is recovered after synthesizing 915 compounds, the scale of a few synthesis campaigns. The in-house HT synthesis approach also involves working with crude mixtures rather than purified solutions, but such mixtures remain compatible with crystallographic, biochemical, and biophysical screening formats.31–33,50Beyond accessing more compounds, Syndirella has the potential to improve the productivity of the resulting experiments. By enabling a reactant-based purchasing strategy, it can increase predicted interaction productivity, that is, the number of unique predicted protein–ligand interactions achievable within a given budget (Fig. 9). In our analyses, this means that for the same expenditure, more compounds can be tested and those compounds are predicted to result in a larger set of unique protein–ligand interactions. This can provide more data points per screening campaign and may increase the likelihood of identifying higher-affinity binders.Syndirella generates rich datasets intrinsically suited for multi-objective optimization,…
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionSyndirella addresses a critical gap in FBDD where current reaction based enumeration tools to produce congeneric series of compounds are not designed to leverage the advantages of HT micro- and nano-scale chemistry platforms. Our analysis across three targets (CHIKV-Mac, EV-A71-2A, and EV-D68-3C-PROA) shows that not only can Syndirella produce congeneric series for SAR analysis that allow for higher diversity by purchasing reactants instead of products, it also could provide a rich dataset to sample binding site interactions. Application to NCS-1 shows how Syndirella allows for direct-to-biology testing for SAR exploration of crystal structure and kinetic data overlap.In conclusion, Syndirella represents a valuable addition to the FBDD toolbox, offering a practical solution for generating diverse, synthetically accessible elaborations while providing rich SAR information through comprehensive exploration of the binding site. Its integration of HT synthesis considerations makes it particularly well-suited for modern drug discovery workflows where speed, cost, and synthetic accessibility are crucial factors.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionFragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) has established itself as an effective method that provides starting points for compound design towards desired activity against the function of a protein.1,2 It operates under the assumption that, in the early hit-to-lead stage, small molecules (<250 Da) are more informative than the larger molecules typical of traditional high-throughput (HT) screening.2,3 Fragment screens usually have a higher hit rate, a higher percentage of interacting atoms (higher ligand efficiency), and more effective sampling of chemical space.4,5 Structural methods can resolve fragments' conformations and interactions, and their simplicity leaves room for development through simple chemistry. This informative fragment dataset provides the foundation for knowledge-based compound design; however, fully utilizing structural information from the whole fragment screen remains challenging and usually only one or a few fragments are considered in designing derivatives.6,7 This is because there are no systematic approaches for routinely advancing information from many fragments to compounds with measurable potency suitable for lead optimization.Drug discovery often relies on iterative Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycles that, while systematic, suffer from fundamental limitations in their ability to always find optimal solutions to the drug discovery problem.8 These sequential approaches do not guarantee convergence to the best possible compound, as they are inherently susceptible to becoming trapped in local solution minima. Each DMTA iteration typically explores only a small subset of chemical modifications around a limited number of the most promising compounds, creating a step-wise optimization process that may miss superior solutions located in distant regions of chemical space.9 This incremental approach can lead to suboptimal drug candidates, as the final compound is heavily dependent on the initial starting points and the specific pathway taken through chemical space, rather than representing a true global optimum.The obvious places to start to implement a more comprehensive exploration strategy for fragment progression are the Design and Make components of the DMTA cycle. For the design component, one of the early priorities with fragment progression is to increase the affinity of the compound by increasing the number of non-covalent interactions with relevant residues.10–12 The occurrence of these productive interactions depends on multiple factors, including appropriate geometric alignment between ligand and protein atoms, conformational accessibility of the bound state, and various experimental conditions.13 One systematic method for fragment progression is to explore structure–activity relationships (SAR) of fragments or fragment-inspired designs through congeneric series—sets of compounds that share a common core structure but differ in their substituents.2,14,15 Although navigating the possible design space is not facile, as the estimated SAR space around a fragment up to 26 heavy atoms encompasses approximately 1013 compounds, many of which lack straightforward synthetic routes.16 If the earliest designs require expensive resourcing, the amount of sampling will be affected with fewer designs tested and the accessible chemical space reduced.17,18 Exploring such vast SAR space requires a fundamental shift in the scale of experiments, moving from traditional single-compound synthesis and testing to massively parallel approaches that can handle hundreds to thousands of compounds simultaneously.19–25To maximally support this massive SAR exploration, high-throughput (HT) micro- and nano-scale chemistry that produces hundreds to thousands of crude reaction mixtures (CRMs),26–30 combined with HT X-ray crystallography based binding site-directed purification strategies,31–34 can be coupled to maximally explore the fragment progression chemical space. This direct-to-biology approach leverages low-cost liquid handling platforms to perform plate-based synthesis while eliminating the need for conventional purification steps. Instead of isolating individual compounds through traditional chromatographic methods, the protein target's binding site serves as a molecular filter, selectively enriching active compounds directly from crude mixtures through affinity-based interactions determined by X-ray crystallography. Critically, because X-ray crystallography resolves the electron density of the bound molecule itself, it provides direct structural proof of which component of a mixture is bound, removing ambiguity as to whether observed binding reflects the desired ligand or a byproduct or reagent in the CRM.This binding site purification strategy, introduced by Grosjean et al.,31 enables the evaluation of thousands of CRMs, where only those with meaningful target affinity are retained and characterized. This integrated approach offers significant advantages over traditional compound procurement and purification workflows. While conventional methods require extensive purification of each individual compound before biological testing, imposing substantial costs and extended timelines that slow iterative DMTA cycles, the binding site purification approach has the potential to bypass these bottlenecks.Recent chemistry advances have significantly improved the feasibility of implementing liquid-handling platforms for HT micro- and nano-scale chemistry, expanding both synthetic tractability and the variety of accessible pharmacophoric space.35 These advances include the development of catalysts for ambient conditions, such as G3 and G4 Buchwald palladium precatalysts that enable diverse cross-coupling reactions36,37 and innovative reactor designs for high-throughput electrochemistry.38 Particularly promising are novel approaches for multi-step library synthesis in continuous flow that incorporate multiple synthetic methodologies, as demonstrated by Pijper et al. who developed an assembly line approach for generating diverse compounds through multi-vectorial exploration.39 These advances make routine use of HT chemistry possible in DMTA cycles, although there has been little leverage by computer-aided drug design (CADD) tools.While the experimental proof-of-principle for HT synthesis and testing CRMs has been shown, there are no CADD tools made to output compound sets specifically to be synthesized via these platforms for FBDD. Current approaches that present a combinatorially produced chemical space by reaction based enumeration such as V-SYNTHES and tools offered by BioSolveIT show experimental success but have been used in the classical approach of presenting a compound set that has been heavily filtered to a manageable set for purchase from make-on-demand catalogs (usually <90 compounds).40–43 While successful in their context, if applied to produce compound sets designed to be synthesized in-house by liquid handling robotics, there are missed opportunities for economies of scale through shared synthetic routes and starting materials.44–46 Furthermore, existing reaction based enumeration typically focus on single-step transformations or limited reaction sets, constraining the discovery space. The feasibility of routinely designing and performing multi-step synthesis has become more attainable from the advancements of computer aided synthesis planning tools such as AiZynthFinder,47,48 ASKCOS,49 and Manifold (https://postera.ai/) which allow for more reliable algorithmic proposal especially for common reactions. There is a clear need for CADD tools that can generate large, diverse libraries of synthetically tractable compounds specifically designed for HT synthesis platforms, while maximizing the exploration of the SAR chemical space around fragment hits.Here, we introduce a new tool Syndirella (Synthesis Directed Elaborations) that presents a candidate elaboration space around a fragment derived scaffold constrained to a set of HT-compat…

elements_zh.methods: 该管道定义合成路线,从化学目录中识别反应物的上层结构,通过组合合成预测产物,并使用 Fragmenstein 执行相对于灵感片段的放置。51 该平台是可调和可扩展的,以适应下游 HT 合成实验的特定功能和偏好。
elements_zh.main_results: Syndirella 产生了多种同属系列,能够探索三种病毒蛋白靶标的结合位点。这些阐述概括了已知的片段相互作用,并引入了与功能相关残基的新相互作用。该平台访问化学空间的不同区域,并启用基于反应物的采购策略,从而在典型的预算限制和目录之外进行更广泛的化学空间探索和更高的预测交互生产力。通过反应物采购可以获得超过 400 种 Syndirella 的详细阐述,而通过直接产品采购只能获得两种。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,Syndirella 系统地生成药效多样化的同属系列,从而能够通过晶体碎片屏幕进行全面的 SAR 探索。这种方法为 HT 化学支持的 SAR 研究提供了一种易于处理的方法。该平台在钙结合蛋白上进行了验证,产生了晶体结构和可测量的结合,与目录采购、劳动力和消耗品相比,内部合成实现了 71% 的成本降低。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对病毒蛋白靶点开发更具成本效益和更全面的 SAR 研究提供信息,从而提高基于片段的药物发现的效率。该平台能够访问化学空间的不同区域并启用基于反应物的采购策略,可以在典型的预算限制内实现更高的预测交互生产力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括它不是随机对照试验,并且结果基于计算预测和内部综合。由于依赖计算方法和需要实验验证,证据强度中等。

One algorithmic method that implements fragment merging and is extensively used throughout our pipeline is Fragmenstein.51 Fragmenstein combines atoms from fragments using structural information to create derivatives that are predicted to adopt the same binding pose as the fragments. Pose generation is performed using the tool Fragmenstein,51 although any pose generation method could be used, whether restrained to the parent fragment pose or not. Through comparison with traditional superstructure search methods, we show how Syndirella accesses distinct regions of chemical space. 2 shows a representative result, where a single fragment-inspired scaffold yields a set of elaborations that share one synthesis route and vary in substituents and pharmacophores. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Cell-Penetrating Receptor Mimic Delivers a Long-Sought Blow Against Enteroviruses by October 13, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Cell-Penetrating Receptor Mimic Delivers a Long-Sought Blow Against Enteroviruses Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Hand, foot, and mouth disease is usually dismissed as a routine childhood illness, yet its most severe forms are caused by two closely related viruses that continue to claim young lives across Asia and beyond. Enterovirus A71, often abbreviated EV-A71, and its frequent companion coxsackievirus A16 are the leading viral culprits behind serious cases of the disease, capable of progressing from fever and blistering rashes to life-threatening brainstem encephalitis, pulmonary edema, and death in infants and small children. Despite decades of research and the deployment of vaccines in some countries, no specific antiviral drug against these pathogens has reached clinical practice, leaving physicians to manage the sickest patients with supportive care alone. A team led by Shijin Wang, Yubin Tang, and colleagues, writing in PLOS Pathogens, now reports a molecule that may change that picture. The researchers describe RMP(R8), an engineered peptide that mimics the part of a human protein called SCARB2, which the viruses use as their essential gateway into cells. In laboratory tests the compound blocked EV-A71 and CV-A16 at remarkably low concentrations, showed an excellent safety profile, and improved survival in a lethal neonatal mouse model of infection. The work also resolves a paradox that has frustrated antiviral developers for roughly a decade, and in doing so proposes a new playbook for drugging virus-receptor interactions that occur deep inside cells rather than on their surfaces. To appreciate why the finding matters, it helps to understand how these viruses gain entry. EV-A71 and CV-A16 belong to the genus Enterovirus within the family Picornaviridae, small non-enveloped viruses whose outer shell is built from four structural proteins arranged with icosahedral symmetry. For enteroviruses of this group, attachment to a surface receptor is only the first act. The truly decisive step, known as uncoating, occurs after the virus has been taken up into the cell, when the protein shell rearranges or releases its RNA genome so replication can begin. SCARB2, a lysosomal membrane protein found abundantly on many human cell types, is the receptor that triggers this uncoating reaction. Structural studies have shown that binding of the virion to SCARB2 destabilizes the capsid, converting the virus into an expanded particle that expels its genome into the cytosol. That mechanism suggests an obvious therapeutic strategy, at least on paper. If a soluble fragment of SCARB2 floating outside the cell could latch onto incoming virus particles and prematurely trip their uncoating switch, the virus would fall apart harmlessly in extracellular fluid. Such receptor decoys have succeeded against other pathogens, and researchers duly built Fc-fusion proteins carrying the extracellular domain of SCARB2. The results were consistently disappointing. The decoys failed to neutralize EV-A71 in meaningful ways, a puzzle that has stood in the literature for some ten years and discouraged further investment in SCARB2-based antivirals. The reason, as the new study makes clear, is that SCARB2 does its critical work not on the cell surface but inside the endosomal and lysosomal compartments, where the acidity and protease environment differ dramatically from conditions outside the cell and where a large, bulky Fc-fusion protein simply cannot follow the virus. The team’s solution was to shrink the receptor to its functional core and smuggle it to where it is needed. Mining the structure of the SCARB2-virion interface, they identified a short stretch of the protein, spanning amino acids W146 through K166, as the minimal region that binds VP2, one of the capsid proteins on the viral shell. They fused this twenty-one-residue binding domain to octa-arginine, a classical cell-penetrating peptide composed of eight positively charged arginine residues. The result is RMP(R8), an intracellular receptor mimetic: small enough to cross cell membranes and enter the cytosol and vesicular compartments, yet retaining the binding surface that the virus itself recognizes. In effect, the molecule impersonates the receptor inside the cell, contacting virus particles at the very stage where extracellular decoys are absent and where premature engagement spells disaster for the pathogen. The numbers reported for the compound are striking. RMP(R8) inhibited EV-A71 with a half-maximal effective concentration of 0.156 micrograms per milliliter, a potent value for a peptide antiviral. Its selectivity index, the ratio comparing the dose that harms host cells with the dose that blocks the virus, exceeded 2003, indicating a wide therapeutic margin. The peptide also dissolved readily in water, an unglamorous but decisive property for any molecule hoping to be formulated, dosed, and distributed clinically. In cultured cells derived from the intestine and the nervous system, tissues that matter most for enterovirus disease, RMP(R8) suppressed infection by genetically divergent EV-A71 isolates as well as by CV-A16, suggesting the activity is not confined to a single laboratory strain but extends across the viral diversity that vaccines and strain-specific antibodies struggle to cover. Mechanistically, the authors traced the compound’s action to the blockage of viral entry. Rather than preventing attachment to the cell surface, RMP(R8) interferes with the intracellular step at which SCARB2 normally catalyzes uncoating. By engaging the virion’s VP2-binding site at the wrong time and place, the mimetic presumably triggers or locks the capsid into a state that cannot deliver its genome productively. This timing explains the failure of the older decoys and the success of the new one: the virus is vulnerable to receptor mimicry only after it has entered the cell, and only a molecule that reaches that compartment can exploit the vulnerability. The concept is generalizable in principle. Any virus that performs its key receptor-dependent step intracellularly, and there are several among the picornaviruses and related families, could in theory be targeted by a cell-penetrating mimetic of the relevant receptor domain. Animal testing provided the strongest evidence that the approach survives contact with a living system. In a lethal neonatal mouse model, the standard challenge assay for EV-A71 pathogenesis, treatment with RMP(R8) significantly increased survival of infected pups following challenge with EV-A71 and with CV-A16 alike. Neonatal mice lack a mature immune system and are exquisitely susceptible to these viruses, so a survival benefit in this setting is a meaningful benchmark for a candidate antiviral. The breadth across two distinct viral species is particularly notable, because cross-species coverage is rare among antivirals that target viral enzymes or capsid pockets, which are easily undermined by a handful of point mutations. Targeting the conserved receptor-binding surface, by contrast, raises the genetic barrier to escape. Considerable work remains between a promising peptide and an approved medicine. RMP(R8) must still demonstrate an acceptable pharmacokinetic profile, stability against proteases, appropriate tissue distribution, and safety in larger animals, and the dosing window in human infection, where treatment would likely begin after symptom onset, will need careful definition. Cell-penetrating peptides also face well-known questions about delivery and clearance in patients. Even so, the study stands out for solving a concrete mechanistic puzzle: it explains why extracellular SCARB2 decoys failed, and it converts that explanation into a working drug candidate with potency, breadth, and in vivo efficacy. For the millions of children at risk of severe hand, foot, and mouth disease each year, and for the clinicians who currently have nothing specific to offer them, an intracellular receptor mimetic that attacks EV-A71 and CV-A16 at their most vulnerable moment represents exactly the kind of targeted therapy the field has been waiting for. It also redraws the boundary of antiviral design, showing that the inside of the cell, long considered hostile territory for receptor-based drugs, can be reached and exploited. news.content: City Voices Trending Hong Kong Business International Racing Lifestyle Showbiz Sport Opinion Games More ePaper City Voices People ArtCan Trending Social Buzz Must Read Hong Kong News Explorer Politics Health Education Business Finance Property Innovation ESG International China World Racing Hong Kong Racing World Racing Analysis Racecourse Entertainment Lifestyle Arts & Culture Wellness Food & Wine Leisure Showbiz Entertainment Gossip Screen & Music Sport Sports Updates Football Basketball Tennis Opinion Editorial Insights Games Crossword HONG KONG NEWS DH urges public to maintain hygiene amid increasing activity of hand, foot and mouth disease NEWS 14-10-2026 19:52 HKT The Department of Health(DH) urged on Wednesday the public to maintain hygiene, as cases of the local hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) increased recently The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the DH will issue letters to schools today, updating them on the latest situation regarding HFMD. Schools and institutions are required to report any outbreak to the CHP immediately. The CHP's latest surveillance data recorded eight outbreaks in institutions and schools, affecting 27 persons, per week in mid-September. The number of HFMD outbreaks increased gradually to 12 outbreaks, 11 outbreaks, and 20 outbreaks per week in the past three weeks. From this Sunday to Tuesday, nine outbreaks affecting 24 persons have been reported. Ninety percent of the outbreaks occurred in Child Care Centers, Kindergartens and primary schools. HFMD is a common disease in children caused by enteroviruses (EVs) such as Coxsackie virus and EV71. HFMD occurs throughout the year in Hong Kong, with the usual peak occurring from May to July and October to December. It usually causes mild symptoms, fever, poor appetite, fatigue, and sore throat, followed by painful mouth sores that may ulcerate. Most people recover without treatment in 7 to 10 days, according to the DH. The department also reminded that alcohol-based handrub should not substitute hand hygiene with liquid soap and water, as alcohol does not effectively kill some viruses causing HFMD. analysis.time: The article was published on 14 Oct 2026 at 19:52 HKT. It reports that HFMD outbreaks have risen over the past three weeks, with nine outbreaks affecting 24 persons reported from Sunday to Tuesday of the current week.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreaks are occurring in Hong Kong, primarily in child‐care centres, kindergartens and primary schools. Surveillance recorded eight outbreaks affecting 27 persons per week in mid‐September, and the recent nine outbreaks involved 24 persons, most of whom are children.
analysis.event: The Department of Health (DH) urged the public to maintain personal hygiene, and the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) issued letters to schools updating them on the rising HFMD activity. Surveillance data show eight outbreaks in mid‐September, increasing to 12, 11 and 20 outbreaks per week over the last three weeks, with nine outbreaks affecting 24 persons reported from Sunday to Tuesday.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Eight to twenty HFMD outbreaks have been recorded weekly, involving 24‐27 reported cases in the most recent periods. About 90% of outbreaks occur in child‐care settings. The DH has not indicated a heightened public‐health emergency, implying the risk remains limited to the affected institutions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: DH has issued a public hygiene reminder and CHP is sending letters to schools; institutions must report any outbreak immediately. Ongoing surveillance continues, but the report provides only outbreak counts from schools and does not include community‐wide case numbers, leaving the full extent of transmission uncertain.

analysis.brief_en: Hong Kong's Department of Health has warned residents to keep up personal hygiene as hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) activity climbs. The Centre for Health Protection reports a rise from eight outbreaks in mid‐September to as many as 20 per week over the past three weeks, with nine outbreaks affecting 24 children reported from Sunday to Tuesday. Most cases occur in child‐care centres, kindergartens and primary schools, accounting for about 90% of outbreaks. DH has sent letters to schools and reminded the public that alcohol‐based hand rubs are not a substitute for soap and water. While surveillance continues, the data cover only institutional reports, so the broader community impact remains unclear.

news.content: Skip to main navigation Login Logout SUBSCRIBE Sign up for FREE daily enews × Menu Magazine Profiles in Business Giving Guide Digital Archives News People In The News Company Database Contact Us Advertise All Events Special Events -A +A VDH: COVID, viruses slowly increasing Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Submitted by tim on Tue, 10/13/2026 - 04:30 Report Timeframe: October 1-October 7, 2026. Current Vermont Department of Health recommendations on preventing COVID-19 by Timothy McQuiston, Vermont Business Magazine The Vermont Department of Health has reported that COVID-19 hospitalizations remain scarce but have edged up in recent weeks. The COVID-19 virus (SARS-CoV-2) remains active in Vermont at the Montpelier, Essex Junction and South Burlington test sites and nationally. Meanwhile, Norovirus and EVD68 have become more pronounced. There was one COVID outbreak reported at a long-term care facility in Orleans County. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a virus that causes respiratory illness similar to the common cold. It sometimes leads to severe breathing issues and outbreaks of neurological disease (acute flaccid myelitis) that causes paralysis. Most people regain some muscle function, but some may have lasting health issues. See most recent test results below. Neither the VDH nor the CDC are any longer reporting COVID fatalities or total cases in Vermont or in the US. The hospitalizations dataset contains day-level data reported from all Vermont hospitals each Tuesday. Reported numbers are subject to correction. Laboratory-confirmed and diagnosed COVID-19 cases and COVID-19 outbreaks must still be reported to the Vermont Department of Health. There was 1 COVID outbreak last week (1 the week before), with 1 in Long-Term Care Facilities and 0 in schools. Outbreaks had disappeared since mid-summer. There have been no school outbreaks even as students have returned to the classroom. Overall, there have been only 6 outbreaks, all in LTC, since the March 2, 2026, report. Duopharma distributes HFMD vaccine All news Top Stories Editors' Picks Stocks Crypto Economics Currencies Commodities Business & Wealth Market Voices Andreas Kristo 15.10.2026 Duopharma secures exclusive distribution rights for HFMD vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Duopharma secures exclusive rights Duopharma Biotech Bhd is expanding its preventive healthcare offerings after its wholly owned unit secured exclusive rights to distribute a hand, foot and mouth disease vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei. The agreement remains subject to regulatory approval in all three markets, while Malaysia still has no HFMD vaccine approved for use. Highlights Duopharma (M) secured exclusive rights to market, sell and obtain approval for the EnVAX-A71 HFMD vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei through an agreement with Enimmune Corp. The agreement is valid for five years in each territory, subject to Duopharma meeting minimum annual order quantities; failure to achieve 70% of the target for two consecutive years allows Enimmune to terminate the contract. Duopharma shares closed down one sen, or 0.90%, at RM1.10 on Thursday, with a market capitalisation of RM1.06 billion. This article was translated from the original. Read the original version by our correspondent here. Scope of the agreement and approval requirements According to The Edge Malaysia, as reported in the group's stock exchange filing on Thursday, the supply agreement was signed between Taiwan's Enimmune Corp and Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned unit of Duopharma Biotech. Under the agreement, Duopharma (M) was granted exclusive rights to advertise, market, sell and obtain marketing approval for the EnVAX-A71 vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei. Under the terms, Duopharma (M) is responsible for obtaining regulatory approval for the vaccine in all three countries. If any country rejects approval for the vaccine, the company's obligations for that country will be terminated. The agreement remains in force in each territory until the fifth anniversary of the launch date in the respective jurisdiction, provided that Duopharma (M) meets the minimum annual order quantity after registration is approved. If the company fails to meet 70% of the minimum annual quantity for two consecutive contract years, Enimmune has the right to terminate the agreement. In a separate statement on Thursday, Duopharma Biotech chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid said the collaboration strengthens the group's vaccine portfolio and helps build a sustainable presence in preventive healthcare. The group also said Enimmune will bear the costs related to Good Manufacturing Practice assessments and provide marketing support for the launch in Malaysia. Public health importance and market impact Duopharma said the agreement aligns with its strategy to expand its biologics portfolio. According to Wan Amir-Jeffery, the group's focus is on bringing specialised vaccines to Malaysia that address unmet needs and complement existing healthcare treatment options. HFMD is an infectious disease that commonly affects children under the age of five, with early symptoms including fever, sore throat and loss of appetite. The disease also causes painful mouth ulcers and rashes on the hands, soles of the feet and buttocks. Duopharma stated that HFMD is a major public health concern because outbreaks occur frequently in Malaysia. The disease is commonly caused by the enteroviruses Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus A71, while EnVAX-A71 is a monovalent vaccine targeting EV71, a strain that can cause severe neurological complications and death among children. There is currently no cure for HFMD, and no vaccine has yet been approved for use in Malaysia. Duopharma shares closed down one sen, or 0.90%, at RM1.10 on Thursday, placing the group's market capitalisation at RM1.06 billion. In our earlier coverage of weakness in Malaysia's stock market, the FBM KLCI was reported to have declined as concerns over US inflation and the direction of interest rates weighed on investor sentiment. We also highlighted selling pressure in technology counters such as YTL Power and ViTrox, as well as continued net selling by foreign institutions, which added pressure to the local market. Under the terms, Duopharma (M) is responsible for obtaining regulatory approval for the vaccine in all three countries. If any country rejects approval for the vaccine, the company's obligations for that country will be terminated. The agreement remains in force in each territory until the fifth anniversary of the launch date in the respective jurisdiction, provided that Duopharma (M) meets the minimum annual order quantity after registration is approved. If the company fails to meet 70% of the minimum annual quantity for two consecutive contract years, Enimmune has the right to terminate the agreement. In a separate statement on Thursday, Duopharma Biotech chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid said the collaboration strengthens the group's vaccine portfolio and helps build a sustainable presence in preventive healthcare. The group also said Enimmune will bear the costs related to Good Manufacturing Practice assessments and provide marketing support for the launch in Malaysia. Public health importance and market impact Duopharma said the agreement aligns with its strategy to expand its biologics portfolio. According to Wan Amir-Jeffery, the group's focus is on bringing specialised vaccines to Malaysia that address unmet needs and complement existing healthcare treatment options. HFMD is an infectious disease that commonly affects children under the age of five, with early symptoms including fever, sore throat and loss of appetite. The disease also causes painful mouth ulcers and rashes on the hands, soles of the feet and buttocks. Duopharma stated that HFMD is a major public health concern because outbreaks occur frequently in Malaysia. The disease is commonly caused by the enteroviruses Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus A71, while EnVAX-A71 is a monovalent vaccine targeting EV71, a strain that can cause severe neurological complications and death among children. There is currently no cure for HFMD, and no vaccine has yet been approved for use in Malaysia. Duopharma shares closed down one sen, or 0.90%, at RM1.10 on Thursday, placing the group's market capitalisation at RM1.06 billion. In our earlier coverage of weakness in Malaysia's stock market, the FBM KLCI was reported to have declined as concerns over US inflation and the direction of interest rates weighed on investor sentiment. We also highlighted selling pressure in technology counters such as YTL Power and ViTrox, as well as continued net selling by foreign institutions, which added pressure to the local market. KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 15): Duopharma Biotech Bhd (KL:DPHARMA) said on Thursday its wholly owned unit has secured exclusive rights to distribute Taiwan-based Enimmune Corp's hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei, subject to regulatory approval in the three countries. According to the group’s bourse filing on Thursday, the supply agreement was signed between Enimmune and Duopharma Biotech's wholly owned unit Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd (DMSB). Under the deal, DMSB is responsible for getting regulatory approval for the EnVAX-A71 Vaccine in the three countries. The deal also grants DMSB exclusive rights to advertise, market, sell and obtain marketing approval for the vaccine. If a country refuses to approve the vaccine, DMSB's obligations in that country are terminated. In a separate statement on Thursday, Duopharma Biotech chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid said: “This partnership is a further step in strengthening our vaccine portfolio and building a sustainable presence in preventive healthcare.” The group said Enimmune will cover costs related to Good Manufacturing Practice assessments and provide marketing support for the Malaysian launch. The agreement will remain in force in each territory until the fifth anniversary of the launch date in the respective jurisdictions, contingent on DMSB fulfilling minimum annual order quantities once registration is approved. If DMSB fails to fulfil 70% of the annual minimum order quantity for two consecutive contract years, Enimmune has the right to terminate the agreement. Niche vaccine for major public health concern Duopharma said the deal aligns with its strategy to expand its biologics portfolio. “Our focus is on bringing niche vaccines to Malaysia that address unmet needs and complement the healthcare options available today,” Wan added. HFMD is a contagious disease that commonly infects children under the age of 5. Early symptoms include fever, sore throat and reduced appetite. It also causes painful mouth sores and rashes on the hands, soles of feet and buttocks. Due to its contagious nature and severity, HFMD is a significant public health concern as outbreaks are common in Malaysia. HFMD is usually caused by enteroviruses Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus A71 (EV71). There is no cure for HFMD and there is currently no vaccine approved for use in Malaysia. The EnVAX-A71 Vaccine is a monovalent inoculation that targets EV71, which is the strain that causes severe neurological complications and fatalities in children. Duopharma shares ended one sen lower or 0.90% at RM1.10 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM1.06 billion. (Updated every 15 mins) BURSA:TECHBASE 0.070 0.00% 43.83x |BURSA:SUPERLN 0.900 ▲2.27% 11.80x |BURSA:LBICAP 0.505 0.00% 11.29x |BURSA:EMETALL 0.440 0.00% 9.47x |BURSA:WELLCHIP 1.060 ▼0.93% 7.61x | BURSA:TECHBASE 0.070 0.00% 43.83x |BURSA:SUPERLN 0.900 ▲2.27% 11.80x |BURSA:LBICAP 0.505 0.00% 11.29x |BURSA:EMETALL 0.440 0.00% 9.47x |BURSA:WELLCHIP 1.060 ▼0.93% 7.61x | Home Duopharma Biotech unit secures HFMD vaccine distribution rights in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Corporate Malaysia Duopharma Biotech unit secures HFMD vaccine distribution rights in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei By Justin Cheng / theedgemalaysia.com 15 Oct 2026, 07:40 pm Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google Enimmune president Chang Che-Wei (left) and Duopharma Biotech chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid at the signing ceremony for the vaccine distribution rights agreement. KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 15): Duopharma Biotech Bhd (KL:DPHARMA) said on Thursday its wholly owned unit has secured exclusive rights to distribute Taiwan-based Enimmune Corp's hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei, subject to regulatory approval in the three countries. According to the group’s bourse filing on Thursday, the supply agreement was signed between Enimmune and Duopharma Biotech's wholly owned unit Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd (DMSB). Under the deal, DMSB is responsible for getting regulatory approval for the EnVAX-A71 Vaccine in the three countries. The deal also grants DMSB exclusive rights to advertise, market, sell and obtain marketing approval for the vaccine. If a country refuses to approve the vaccine, DMSB's obligations in that country are terminated. In a separate statement on Thursday, Duopharma Biotech chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid said: “This partnership is a further step in strengthening our vaccine portfolio and building a sustainable presence in preventive healthcare.” The group said Enimmune will cover costs related to Good Manufacturing Practice assessments and provide marketing support for the Malaysian launch. The agreement will remain in force in each territory until the fifth anniversary of the launch date in the respective jurisdictions, contingent on DMSB fulfilling minimum annual order quantities once registration is approved. If DMSB fails to fulfil 70% of the annual minimum order quantity for two consecutive contract years, Enimmune has the right to terminate the agreement. Niche vaccine for major public health concern Duopharma said the deal aligns with its strategy to expand its biologics portfolio. “Our focus is on bringing niche vaccines to Malaysia that address unmet needs and complement the healthcare options available today,” Wan added. HFMD is a contagious disease that commonly infects children under the age of 5. Early symptoms include fever, sore throat and reduced appetite. It also causes painful mouth sores and rashes on the hands, soles of feet and buttocks. Due to its contagious nature and severity, HFMD is a significant public health concern as outbreaks are common in Malaysia. HFMD is usually caused by enteroviruses Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus A71 (EV71). There is no cure for HFMD and there is currently no vaccine approved for use in Malaysia. The EnVAX-A71 Vaccine is a monovalent inoculation that targets EV71, which is the strain that causes severe neurological complications and fatalities in children. Duopharma shares ended one sen lower or 0.90% at RM1.10 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM1.06 billion.
